findings.title: Preserve readable primary-button contrast across theme and hover states
findings.description: Enabled primary actions retain hard-coded white foreground while dark mode changes their accent background to #81ab97, giving 2.5593:1 contrast for ordinary 12-14px labels. Independently, .button:hover:not(:disabled) has greater specificity than .button.primary and replaces its background with surface-2; primary:hover only applies brightness, so a light-theme hover gives approximately 1.1237:1 white-on-pale contrast. These affect the shared primary action style, including save configuration and publish-sharing confirmation, rather than only decorative text or disabled controls.
evidence: web/styles.css:204-213: generic enabled hover replaces background; primary sets accent background and white foreground; primary hover sets only brightness(0.94).
web/styles-responsive.css:10 and :49: both system-dark and explicit-dark accent is #81ab97.
web/components/ProviderSettings.tsx:337-346: enabled save-configuration button uses button primary.
web/components/PluginSharing.tsx:439-471: enabled publish-sharing confirmation uses button primary.

Fresh source-wide inspection found no later primary foreground/background override. Other solid accent backgrounds are project/loading dots without text. Send-button has separate #5d7560 background and white icon, measured 5.0253:1.
reproduction: Select explicit dark theme, or system theme while the system prefers dark, and enable any primary action such as Save configuration. Its source-derived foreground/background are #ffffff/#81ab97.

In light theme, hover any enabled button.primary. The generic hover selector (0,3,0) outranks .button.primary (0,2,0), so the background becomes #f0f2f0 while text remains white; both are then filtered by brightness(0.94).
findings.recommendation: Add a semantic on-accent foreground token used by the shared .button.primary rule, preserving white in light mode and a dark foreground such as #1c201f in both explicit/system dark mode (6.4318:1 against #81ab97). Also set background: var(--accent) explicitly in .button.primary:hover:not(:disabled) so the higher-specificity generic hover cannot substitute surface-2. Check the shared selector states, not individual call sites.
findings.verification: Source and CSS-cascade inspection plus an independent relative-luminance calculation; no browser run, screenshot, automated test, or production interaction was performed. Hover was initially reported by the parent reviewer and independently confirmed against current source and recalculated here.

method: Fresh independent static audit of exactly the 128 non-test paths in groups.web from the frozen round5 inventory, reassigned by the parent after the separate reviewer took all 65 web/tests paths. Read the full current content of all assigned TypeScript/TSX modules and manually traced semantic behavior, async and visit ownership, authentication and connection transitions, durable unknown-operation recovery, draft preservation, privilege/approval and external-sharing confirmation boundaries, bounded rendering and media, file/Git operations, accessibility controls, and user-visible outcomes. Read all seven assigned CSS files plus entry HTML, compiler/bundler configuration, and the current verification document; the latter was reviewed as current documentation, not relied on as prior audit evidence. Large tool outputs that were truncated were reread in bounded chunks. No generated coverage claim, no assumption that a text/AST scan proves semantic coverage, and no test files are claimed by this report. Initial verification checked all 1880 inventory file SHA-256 values with no mismatch at 2026-10-27T03:17:11.9917960Z; final verification checked all 1880 file hashes again and recomputed the canonical scripts/snapshot.mjs digest and source-name inventory. Audit-only commands did not execute tests/builds, change product source, deploy, run paid inference, access external MCP, or access the personal CODEX_HOME runtime. Findings were reported promptly while completing scope.
